report:
Finding: Model B appears to have a stronger instruction/algorithmic/step‑by‑step prior (e.g., chain‑of‑thought and transform/edit behaviors), especially at the beginning of the sequence, compared to Model A.

Why I think this:
- Difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across almost all layers, a common signature of a changed BOS prior as seen in instruction/RLHF-tuned checkpoints.
- Patchscope injections consistently produce procedural/instructional patterns: numbered lists, “->” mappings, meta‑prompts (“What is the first letter…”, “So now we have… the next step is:”), code-ish fragments (“if (length > 1)”, “print(‘hello’)”, “bits -> 1/0”), and identity/rename transforms (“you -> you”, “hello -> hello”). This is characteristic of models tuned to follow instructions and lay out steps.
- Logit-lens at pos0 in mid/high layers leans toward imperative/advisory vocabulary (“Do”, “Check”, “optimize”, “ensure”, “strive”, “adopt”, “adhere”, “proactive”, “carefully”, “wary”), which fits guideline/procedural text. Tokens at later positions include discourse connectors (“Later”, “mention”, “refer”) typical of expository/instructional style.

Caveats:
- Some topical tokens (e.g., “surgeon”, “law”, “Royals”) appear in the logit lens, but they’re not coherent enough to support a specific domain shift. The clearest, repeated signal is procedural/instruction-following behavior, not a particular subject area.

Conclusion: The evidence supports a behavioral/objective difference where Model B is more instruction/chain‑of‑thought/transform‑oriented at BOS (and propagating into subsequent tokens), while Model A is closer to a generic web‑text prior.
